description: WIDE-nb panel at n=4096 with TF32 trailing — the one regime where widening nb PAYS. A sibling proved widening the panel block-width nb conserves total O(n^3) work by MOVING it from the panel kernel into a WIDER trailing GEMM, and that loses at n=512 because the tight factor budget (~1.2e-3) forces the trailing GEMM to FP32 (cutlass SIMT). BUT at n=4096 the budget is LOOSE (~1e-2), so the wider trailing GEMM can run TF32 (cutlass TENSOR-CORE, ~2x faster than FP32-SIMT). So at n=4096 wide-nb shifts work from the serial FP32 panel into a fast TF32 tensor-core GEMM — a net win the tight-budget shapes can't get. Test n=4096 (currently cluster ~31k): single-CTA blocked panel with WIDE nb (64/128/256, needs MAXCB raised + the brief-31 ldv!=cb artifact) + uniform TF32 trailing, A/B vs the cluster. Fewer/wider panels + tensor-core trailing. FP32 panel; keep n!=4096 as parent. No 'stream' substring.

NAIVE wide cb: n=4096 cluster panel cb=16->64 + uniform TF32 trailing (CL_MAXCB=128, all-cluster). REGRESSION: shape6 n=4096 68334->96436us (+41%). Profile: trailing GEMM DID get 4x cheaper (16ms->4ms) but cluster panel's O(m*cb^2) in-SMEM apply blew up 39->278ms. geomean 8441 vs parent 8194.

NAIVE wide cb=32 (sweep point). shape6 70929us vs parent 68334 (+3.8%); geomean 8221. Curve cb=16->68334, cb=32->70929, cb=64->96436: monotonically worse -- naive cb-widening of the cluster panel LOSES at every cb.

OUTER/INNER nb=64 (narrow ib=16 cluster panel + wide combined-WY rank-64 TF32 trailing; block wy_tfactor). Clean benchmark (low contention): shape6 n=4096 71277us vs parent 68334 (+4%); geomean 8272. The decoupling keeps the panel cheap and shrinks the trailing, but the combined-T (Gram+WY recurrence) cancels it.

FINAL (kept): n=4096 OUTER/INNER ib=16/nb=128 (narrow inner cluster panel + wide combined-WY rank-128 TF32 tensor-core trailing via new wy_tfactor kernel); n!=4096 = parent (n=2048 tested -> ~parity, reverted). Clean benchmark shape6 n=4096 69678us vs parent 68334 (+2%, best outer/inner config); geomean 8265.74 vs parent 8194.36. nsys medians: panel_cluster ~42ms (dominant, ~unchanged), wy_tfactor ~7.7ms, wide trailing efficient. MEASURED VERDICT: wide-nb trailing genuinely shrinks (~11ms saved) but combined-T (Gram+serial WY recurrence at B=2) + within-block trailing cancels it -> ~parity/slightly-negative at n=4096. Tests+diff_correctness CLEAN.

MEASURED OUTCOME: wide-nb at n=4096 lands ~parity/slightly-negative vs the parent cluster, NOT a win. Final kept config (n=4096 outer/inner ib=16/nb=128): clean benchmark shape6 n=4096 69678us vs parent 68334 (+2%); geomean 8265.74 vs parent 8194.36. n!=4096 kept = parent.

WHAT I TESTED (all 22 tests + diff_correctness guard CLEAN every trial; n=4096 dense scaled_factor_residual 0.59<1.0, uniform TF32 trailing safe):
1) NAIVE single-width cb-widening of the cluster panel LOSES monotonically: shape6 cb=16->68334, cb=32->70929, cb=64->96436us. nsys (contention-immune medians) shows WHY -- the trailing GEMM genuinely gets ~4x cheaper (16ms->4ms, confirming the brief's mechanism) BUT the cluster panel's O(m*cb^2) columnwise in-SMEM apply blows up (39ms->278ms at cb=64). The panel growth dwarfs the trailing savings.
2) OUTER/INNER decoupling (the structural fix): narrow ib=16 inner cluster panel (panel stays cheap ~42ms) + accumulate a WIDE combined compact-WY T per nb-block and apply ONE rank-nb TF32 tensor-core trailing GEMM. New wy_tfactor kernel builds the combined-T from the Gram. Correct + clean. nb sweep: nb=64 +4%, nb=128 +2% (best). nsys medians (~60ms vs parent ~59ms): panel_cluster ~42ms (70%, DOMINANT, ~unchanged), wy_tfactor combined-T ~7.7ms, Gram ~2.3ms, within-block rank-16 trailing ~5.6ms, beyond-block wide rank-128 trailing ~1.2ms. The wide trailing saves ~11ms but the combined-T construction (Gram + SERIAL WY recurrence, bounded by B=2) + within-block trailing + ~3ms higher panel cancel it.
3) ib sweep: ib=16 keeps the panel cheap (median 87us); ib=32 doubles it (242us) -- ib MUST stay narrow.
4) wy_tfactor variants: block-barrier (7.6ms, best), 32-lane-warp (7.0ms), K=16-cluster-parallel form_wy_cluster (28ms, WORSE -- cluster.sync + rank-0 serial recurrence). All bounded by the serial-over-columns recurrence at tiny batch.
5) n=2048 B=8 (brief's 'also test'): outer/inner ALSO ~parity (nsys ~26.9ms vs parent ~27ms). The combined-T is cheaper at B=8 (wy_tfactor ~2.8ms, 4x better parallelized than B=2) but the wide-trailing win is again canceled by the higher panel + within-block trailing. Reverted to parent (not a clear win).

KEY INSIGHT FOR NEXT BRIEFS: the n=4096 (and n=2048) bottleneck is the CLUSTER PANEL itself (~42ms = 70% of GPU time), NOT the trailing GEMM. The brief's premise 'shift work panel->trailing' cannot win because (a) widening cb makes the panel WORSE, and (b) the decoupled wide-trailing saves ~11ms but the combined-T machinery costs ~10ms. OPEN DIRECTIONS not reachable under this brief: (i) attack the cluster panel's serial in-SMEM apply directly (it is SIMT/CUDA-core; a 2-level micro-panel structure INSIDE the cluster like the single-CTA kernel has, or a tensor-core block-apply, could cut the dominant 42ms); (ii) a cheaper combined-T -- the blocked/recursive LARFT (reuse the inner ib*ib T_i's + cuBLAS cross-Gram coupling) to cut the 7.7ms serial WY recurrence, which alone would tip outer/inner to ~10% positive; (iii) overlap the combined-T build with the next block's inner panels (the wy_tfactor is on the critical path serially); (iv) reduce within-block trailing by not splitting (apply the wide trailing to ALL remaining columns incl. within-block via the combined-T, eliminating the rank-16 within-block GEMMs). The new wy_tfactor + the runtime-ldc cluster (cb up to 128) + the all-cluster mhyb plumbing are reusable artifacts for any of these. CONTENTION NOTE: the fleet was heavily loaded; raw benchmark geomeans were inflated up to ~1.6x (n=2048 sentinel) -- I leaned on nsys per-kernel MEDIANS x instances as the contention-immune comparison throughout, with clean-benchmark confirmation where the n=2048 sentinel showed low contention.
